surfaces.part: large red mushroom cap (upper left cluster)

answer.evidence: The main body is the scattered cluster of red mushrooms. The largest cap (rows 9-16) has a widening and narrowing width profile (3,4,5,6,7,9,8,7,5), which reads as a domed ellipse, followed by a dark underside row and a short pale stem at rows 17-19. The lower cluster (rows 23-27) has the same cap and stem structure. The smaller mushrooms are only 2-3 rows tall and are drawn as small caps over stems. The grass tufts are decor. The ring is sparse and loosely drawn, but the caps show top surfaces with stems below, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny scatter of about 6 red-capped mushrooms in a loose ring, with only 15 distinct colours in total. It is much smaller than the references and far less detailed. The tile-based facts give 0 because it is smaller than a full tile, so I judged by eye. Each cap has roughly 3 steps (dark red, red, a white dot highlight), and the stems are plain pale blobs. There is no visible grass, soil or leaf grain around the ring, so the 2x2 tile footprint is mostly empty. The 11% near-neutral share of dark edge pixels suggests the outlines are mostly tinted, but the shapes are so small that this barely shows. Next to the references, which have 5-6 green steps, clumped leaf texture and tinted dark outlines, it looks thinner and more sticker-like. Even allowing for a sparse prop, the shading is shallow and the ring lacks the ground grain and tufts that would make it sit in the grass. A careful artist would not accept it beside the references.
